Resale value of used cameras and lenses

Camera gear keeps its value better than most electronics, but a single problem such as fungus in a lens can make an item nearly worthless. Check these points before you pay.

Updated 2026-10-12 · by FlipLens

What drives the price of a camera body

  • Exact model: generations of the same line differ a lot in value.
  • Shutter count: how many photos the camera has taken. A high count lowers the value; many cameras let you read it from the files or the menu.
  • Sensor and screen: scratches, dead pixels and dust that will not clean.
  • Completeness: battery, charger, strap, caps and box.
  • Region and language: some imported models have different menus or warranty terms.

What drives the price of a lens

  • Mount: the same focal length exists for different mounts (for example Canon RF and EF, Sony E/FE, Nikon Z and F). Compare only the same mount.
  • Optical condition: fungus, haze, separation and deep scratches seriously reduce the value. Shine a light through the lens from the back.
  • Mechanics: autofocus works, zoom and focus rings are smooth, aperture blades are clean and dry.
  • Version: many lenses exist in several versions (for example with or without stabilisation).

Common mistakes

  • Comparing a lens with the same focal length but a different mount or version.
  • Not testing autofocus on a body.
  • Missing fungus because the lens was not checked against light.
  • Ignoring the shutter count on a body that looks clean.

Quick checklist

  • Model, mount and version written down.
  • Lens checked against light for fungus and haze.
  • Body powers on, takes a photo, shutter count known if possible.
  • Battery and charger included.

Questions

How do I check a used lens for fungus?

Shine a bright light through the lens from the back and look for thread-like patterns, spots or a milky haze inside the glass.

Does shutter count matter when reselling?

Yes. Buyers compare it with the expected life of the shutter for that model, so a low count helps the price.
